epic.title: program(migrate): read-only analyzer, module alias, five-file generation, honest report without percentages, corpus harness manifest
epic.body:
## Scope
`keld migrate` (reserved today), the module alias, the five generated files, the report format and the corpus manifest for real apps. Live: keld-guard manifest parser (64 KiB, unique keys, deny fix-text that prints the exact patch), KEL-74 scorer, KEL-237 lifecycle corpus runner pattern, KEL-215 addon evidence rows, the scratchpad demand scan (prototype of the analyzer).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters + panel)
- Analyzer is a read-only Rust verb: lexical, import-binding-aware scan of JS/TS/Vue plus static parsing of package.json/tsconfig/bunfig/electron-builder/forge configs; never evaluates app code; reports KEL-127's four blocker classes separately; emits reversible changes only after authorization (`--write`).
- The report prints static coverage COUNTS by status (✔/▲/✘/unclassified) labelled "static estimate, not a compatibility score"; a KEL-74 claim line appears only for committed corpus members. Arch 04 §1's sample `compat score: 91%` contradicts §4/KEL-74 and must be fixed in the same PR (also arch 07 §4's `keld_migrate_analyze` row).
- Module alias: a package.json dependency whose key is `electron` (npm: alias once published; file:/link: in dev) so every resolver sees `node_modules/electron` as the shim; tsconfig paths is editor/type mapping only (the refuter re-ran the probe: paths does NOT reach a node_modules dependency's require); the `bunfig.toml [alias]` wording in arch 04 §2 is a spec defect. Open: X03 proposes a Bun preload plugin for the five subpath specifiers — decide one owner (X02-A1).
- `--write` seeds `keld.permissions.jsonc` with literal-only grants through the live vocabulary; `windows.<w>.channels` has no live evaluator (blocker shared with F04-A1); no recorder exists.
- Boot facts are host-published at spawn (panel consensus); blocking pre-ready CALLs wait on PANEL-P1.
- Corpus harness: a new manifest (`electron-apps-v0`, panel product) reusing KEL-237's schema and runner pattern, pinned by upstream commit + canonical bytes; analyzer counts are leads attached to rows, never cells.

decision_tickets.title: One module-alias owner: package.json `electron` dependency alias (X02) vs a Bun preload plugin for the five Electron specifiers (X03)
decision_tickets.question: The refuter proved tsconfig paths does not reach a node_modules dependency's `require("electron")`; a package.json dependency alias does on Bun 1.4.2. X03 proposes a Bun plugin to also cover `electron/main|renderer|common|utility`. Recommendation: package.json alias as the single runtime resolver (bundler-neutral) with package `exports` for the subpaths; a plugin only if exports cannot express them. Decide and fix the arch 04 §2 bunfig wording.

coverage_gaps.problem: PANEL-D12 and X02-T4 score an install cell but no ticket defines it: MAP states no .app/DMG exists, KEL-141 (prebuilt CLI+host distribution) is Backlog and KEL-103 In Progress (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06), and X02-T4 runs cells through `keld dev`.

edge_problems.problem: Missing gates: the proof ticket is blocked only by X02-T3 and X01-T2. It consumes none of the implementation it scores and neither PANEL-P1 (sync dialog outcome) nor PANEL-P3 (denominator draft). X01-T2 (lifecycle-family recorder) is not a real gate — product cells reuse the KEL-237 runner pattern, not the recorder.

Wrong gate and missing gate. F01-A4 ('where does userData live under STRICT') does not gate a LegacySandboxOff first proof. The artifact F01-T4 actually consumes — the pre-ready call list / descriptor field set — is produced by PANEL-P3 (MAP: 'unspecified until E1 lists the pre-ready calls'), which gates nothing. The epic also says F01-T4 itself 'lists pre-ready calls', so the producer is ambiguous.

hidden_coupling.coupling: The unsaved-prompt cell couples three atoms with no edges between them. draw.io sets modifiedModalOpen=true (:866) and then calls showMessageBoxSync (:876) inside an async ipcMain listener; if F06-T2's SCAFFOLDED throw fires, the flag is never cleared and every later close is ignored by the guard at :853 — the window can never close. F02-T3 AC1 and F06-T2 AC4 are mutually exclusive for a modified document.
hidden_coupling.fix: New atom 'blocking host CALL from a Bun role' (transport ticket) with edges PANEL-P1 → transport → F06-T2(sync) → X02-T4(close cell); F02-T3 AC1 split into unmodified/modified. If P1 fails, a recorded decision 'draw.io = config + 1 edit'.

hidden_coupling.coupling: Channel grants ↔ migrate. The runtime boundary (enumerated el:<channel>) is only as good as the list migrate emits; F04-T3 carries a migrate AC ('el:* is refused by migrate'), X02-T3 seeds windows.<w>.channels which the guard parses and ignores today, and the list for draw.io is derivable from main-side ipcMain registrations (25 literals) but not from the preload, which forwards page-chosen names.
hidden_coupling.fix: New explicit rule owned by F04-A1: 'grant list source = main-side literal ipcMain registrations; non-literal registration is reported unenumerable'. Edge X02-T3 ← F04-A1; move the migrate AC from F04-T3 to X02-T3.

That is a boot fact delivered at spawn (F01-T4 / KEL-75 no-inherited-env) and a migrate output not present in X02-T3's file list. If it is absent, the boot-time checkForUpdates runs (:2092-2100) and F09-T1's 'typed error on explicit check' fires at activation.
hidden_coupling.fix: Name the declared-role-environment field and its schema owner; add it to X02-T3 outputs and to F01-T4's payload; F09-T1 AC covers both env-present and env-absent boots.

hidden_coupling.coupling: F01-T5 AC3 makes requestSingleInstanceLock() without a config declaration a typed diagnostic; draw.io quits when the call returns false (:1718-1722). Whether the proof app boots therefore depends on migrate emitting the declaration, which is listed in X02-T3 but not edged.
hidden_coupling.fix: Edge X02-T3 ← F01-T5 (declaration key) and an X02-T4 activation precondition.

hidden_coupling.coupling: X02-T3's byte-identical artefact includes keld.build.ts 'per F09-T2', whose schema has no text anywhere (KEL-15 body is only a brief). Changing the build schema later silently invalidates the golden artefact that defines the generator.

refuter_verdicts_batch1.lens: Keld invariants, ownership and reuse (four uniques; default-deny never defaulted to allow; no Electron-isms in core/ipc; no parallel owners; reuse KEL-74/237/102/140/72/75/97/136; measured performance; spec+Linear gate; KEL-127 delegated direction). Verified against origin/main d150a14 files, KEL-127/KEL-17/KEL-19 Linear bodies (fetched 2026-10-06), the scratchpad corpus clones, and five Bun 1.4.2 probes re-run or newly written in the scratchpad (alias-probe, bunfig-probe, sync-probe, starve2, park-probe, file-alias-probe).

verdicts.reason: The direction (a package.json dependency alias so node_modules/electron IS the shim) is confirmed for the Bun resolver, but the specific `npm:` form has an unmet precondition and the non-Bun resolvers were never exercised. Confirmed: bunfig `[alias]` is still inert on Bun 1.4.2 (bunfig-probe loads npm electron@44.5.1 from the install cache and fails on `app`), so arch 04 §3's note holds. Confirmed by a new probe (scratchpad prototypes/file-alias-probe): with `"electron": "file:../shim"` bun install links node_modules/electron -> shim, and app ESM `import 'electron'`, the `electron/main` subpath via an `exports` map, a CJS `require('electron')` from a node_modules dependency, and an ESM dep all resolve to the shim. Refuting facts for the `npm:` form: @keld/electron is not published anywhere (arch 06 §2: 'no npm wrapper is currently shipped'; product-status.tsv row package.keld-electron = partial), and the real package is not installable standalone — `packages/@keld/electron/src/app.ts:8` imports `../../api/src/app.ts` outside the package, so `file:` to the real package fails at runtime ('Cannot find module ../../api/src/link.ts'). tsc and webpack resolution were not tested by the author or by me.
verdicts.evidence: packages/@keld/electron/package.json exports only '.'; packages/@keld/electron/src/app.ts:8 cross-package relative import; docs/architecture/06-runtime-and-tooling.md §2 'Target distribution (not implemented): an @keld/cli npm package'; docs/engineering/product-status.tsv line 14; scratchpad probes: prototypes/bunfig-probe (fails), prototypes/alias-probe main2.ts ({app:keld-shim,cjsDep:keld-shim,esmDep:{def,named}=keld-shim}), prototypes/file-alias-probe/app sub.ts ({app:file-shim,main:file-shim}), app2 (ts shim via file: -> dep resolves), app3 (real @keld/electron via file: -> module-not-found).
verdicts.correction: State the mechanism as 'a package.json dependency whose key is `electron` (npm: alias once @keld/electron is published; `file:`/`link:` for monorepo/dev)', and add two preconditions as owned work: (1) make @keld/electron self-contained (depend on a published @keld/api or inline the link client) — owner KEL-72/KEL-19 distribution; (2) publish `./main`, `./renderer`, `./common` subpath exports. Cheapest settling experiment: in file-alias-probe add `tsc --noEmit` with moduleResolution bundler/node16 and a minimal webpack build with target electron-main; record whether `electron` resolves to node_modules/electron (expected yes: webpack electron-* targets externalize `electron`, so runtime resolution governs — [inference]). Drop bunfig.toml from migrate output or amend arch 04 §2 (see extra finding).

verdicts.reason: KEL-127 body (fetched 2026-10-06) says verbatim: 'A future migration analyzer starts read-only, reports compatibility/security/engine/native-dependency blockers separately and emits reviewable reversible changes only after authorization.' Arch 07 §4 lists `keld_migrate_analyze` as read-only. `KeldErrorObject{code,message,cause?,fix,docs}` and `DoctorFinding{label,ok,detail,error?}` exist in keld-cli and are the shape MCP keld_doctor already emits, so a Rust verb reusing them is the one-owner path. Zettlr forge.config.js:1-32 does `require('child_process')` and `spawn(...)` inside the config module, confirming 'never execute app configs'. Receiver-blind false positives are real: scan_electron_usage.py uses regex `<webview|webviewTag` and draw.io's 7 hits are all `webviewTag: false` (electron.js:728,1090,1407,2210,3087) plus `will-attach-webview` at 2223.
verdicts.evidence: Linear KEL-127 §'Release/adoption evidence, not feature count'; docs/architecture/07-agent-experience.md:90; crates/keld-cli/src/error_object.rs:11-23; crates/keld-cli/src/doctor.rs:43-53; scratchpad scan_electron_usage.py:64; corpus/drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js; corpus/zettlr/forge.config.js:1,32. Cargo.lock: serde_json and toml present, no YAML or JS-parser crate.
verdicts.correction: Three additions are required for the atom to be correctly scoped. (1) Spec gate: KEL-17 is Done with AC '`keld migrate` UX specified (input, output, report format)' but no docs/specs file exists and arch 04 §1 is the only UX text — a new approved spec per docs/agents/spec-template.md must precede any ticket; label the atom 'spec' not 'task'. (2) Code/spec drift: arch 04 §1's flow (`keld migrate` = analyze → generate → alias → report) and arch 06 §2's verb row ('analyzer + config generator') make generation the default; the read-only default with `--write` changes both and must be fixed in the same PR. (3) Dependency gate: Zettlr ships electron-builder YAML; no YAML crate is in Cargo.lock, so either YAML configs are reported as 'manual (unparsed)' or a workspace-pinned YAML dependency passes the dependency review gate. tsconfig.json is JSONC — reuse keld-guard's comment stripper by exposing it, not a second stripper.

verdicts.reason: All cited contradictions are real in the tree: arch 04 §1 sample prints 'compat score: 91% — expected to run' and '✔ supported now: 42/47 call sites'; arch 04 §4 says 'Public percentages require a committed denominator … MUST NOT treat a partial measurement as 100% compatibility'; compat-scoreboard.md rule 4 fixes the only claim shape; evidence.rs `score` formats exactly `{passed}/{n} of {panel} corpus {id}@{digest} ({kind})` (lines 813-819), gates `unweighted_percent` on `product_corpus_is_documented_committed`, and `DOCUMENTED_COMMITTED_PRODUCT_CORPORA` is `&[]` (line 1422). Only `score` constructs `Scoreboard`.
verdicts.evidence: docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md §1 and §4; docs/engineering/compat-scoreboard.md rules 1-4; crates/keld-compat/src/evidence.rs:795-825, 1420-1430; crates/keld-compat/AGENTS.md ('MUST NOT add … a percentage/`complete` that lacks a committed product corpus').
verdicts.correction: Widen the same-PR fix set: arch 07 §4's `keld_migrate_analyze` row says 'returns compat report (score, per-API status, fix list)' and must lose 'score'; arch 04 §1's '42/47 call sites' fraction is also a denominator-shaped claim from a static estimate and should become the proposed per-status counts. The keld-compat AGENTS line 'Corpus score = release gate' stays correct only for KEL-74 `score` output.

verdicts.reason: Policy content is confirmed: arch 03 §3 says `keld migrate seeds the manifest from static analysis`; arch 03 §2 and keld-guard make host-less globs inert and `parse_manifest` is the single decoder (64 KiB, unique keys, KELD-GUARD005/017); `DenyReason::fix` already owns the 'Add a grant at `<ptr>` / Append "<req>" to `<ptr>`' wording (lib.rs:338-359) with `json_pointer_for`; arch 05 (research 214 Table 5) puts dialog-selected paths as added scopes after a host dialog flow, not static grants; evaluate is generic over `app.<group>.<action>` string arrays so seeded `app.net.connect`/`app.shell.open` round-trip. Corpus literals are as claimed (draw.io getPath userData/documents at electron.js:58,3796,4175; Zettlr 40 getPath sites, spawn `shell:true` at get-program-version.ts:35, importer/index.ts:128, run-shell-command.ts:21).

A seeded `app.fs.read: ["$APPDATA/**"]` therefore makes the one live guarded fs op unusable until host `$VAR` resolution lands (arch 03 §2 'Destination: $VARS resolved by the host' — owner not named in the tree; explicit unknown). verdicts.reason: The sync-probe proves only that `Atomics.wait` returns on Bun's main thread after a worker notify; it does not prove a host round-trip can complete while parked. A refined probe (scratchpad prototypes/starve2, Bun 1.4.2) shows the park starves the same-thread event loop: a socket write issued before the park was delivered at 281.5 ms (park ended 280.2 ms) and a 10 ms timer fired at 281.8 ms. The only kipc transport is `@keld/kipc` transport.ts (`DirectedReader.receive` is async, runs on the thread that imported it, i.e. the Bun main thread), so a main-thread blocking CALL can never receive its reply over the existing link. The 'worker-fed SharedArrayBuffer' therefore requires a worker that owns its own kipc connection — a second authenticated session per role, which the host does not admit today (arch 06 §2: 'the v0 echo listener admits exactly one authenticated session') and which is a principal-minting/link-ownership change (KEL-75/KEL-97/KEL-136), i.e. architecture per root AGENTS.md, not a facade detail. park-probe additionally shows the host side stalls after 8192 B while the client is parked (bytesSeenDuringPark 0), so lifecycle Events queue behind any sync call.

verdicts.correction: Split the atom. Part 1 (boot facts) survives: isPackaged, resourcesPath, path catalog and the single-instance verdict are host-known before spawn (host registers the OS singleton first) and can ride a host-owned env/blob next to KELD_APP_LINK (role.rs env injection); `protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged` has no return value and can be buffered until the link is up. Single-instance lock itself must be host-owned (OS mutex/socket) so the facade only reads a verdict.
